record.paper_title: Understanding Solar Flares and Energetic Events: Open questions, observational requirements, and instrumental needs over the coming decade
record.context_brief: Unified solar and stellar flare framework
record.original_question: How can spatially resolved solar-flare observations be combined with unresolved observations of diverse stellar flares, including superflares, to build a common framework that constrains flare position on the stellar disk, flaring-area size, coronal mass ejection identification and characterization, and flare energetics across stars?

evidence.quote: • How do we improve our understanding of the physics of ﬂares by combining spatially resolved solar ﬂare observations with ﬂares observed from a diverse stellar populations (including superﬂares)? Can we provide a framework to constrain and understand factors in stellar ﬂares such as: the position of the ﬂare on the stellar disk, the sizes of ﬂaring areas, the identiﬁcation and characterisation of CMEs, and ﬂare energetics [77–80].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a unified quantitative framework that combines two classes of flare observations into a single inference scheme:

(a) spatially resolved solar flare observations, in which the location, geometry, time evolution, and multi-wavelength emission of a flare on the solar disk can be measured directly; and

(b) spatially unresolved observations of flares on other stars (including superflares with bolometric energies up to roughly 10^36 erg), in which only disk-integrated time series and spectra are available.

Within this framework, propose explicit forward models, observables, and inversion procedures that simultaneously constrain the following quantities for an arbitrary stellar flare event observed only as disk-integrated data:

1. The position of the flare on the visible stellar disk (e.g., a center-to-limb angle or projected coordinates), inferred from limb-darkening signatures, rotational modulation, and time-dependent line profiles.

2. The size (area) of the flaring region as a function of time, inferred from the relation between continuum/line flux, blackbody-equivalent temperature, and filling factor.

3. The identification and characterization (mass, velocity, kinetic energy, geometry) of any associated coronal mass ejection, inferred from blue-shifted absorption/emission features, dimming signatures, and multi-band light-curve morphology.

4. The total flare energetics, including the partition among thermal, non-thermal, radiative, and kinetic components, calibrated against the spatially resolved solar case.

Specifically, formulate scaling relations and statistical priors, calibrated on the resolved solar dataset, that allow the four quantities above to be extracted from unresolved stellar flare observations with quantified uncertainties, and demonstrate that the framework reproduces solar flare ground truth when the Sun is treated as a star.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a forward-looking research program rather than a fully posed mathematical theorem. While partial progress exists on individual components (Sun-as-a-star analyses, superflare statistics, stellar CME signatures via Doppler-shifted lines, area-temperature degeneracies), no complete unified framework jointly constraining flare position, area, CME properties, and energetics across the solar–stellar regime has been established as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Understanding Solar Flares and Energetic Events (white paper)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions about combining resolved solar and unresolved stellar flare observations as a future research need.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open research direction for the coming decade.
